Finite-indexed intersection ⋂_{j∈J}A_j in joint independence is an iterated instance of ordinary set intersection of arbitrary subsets, used in topology and binary independence. Empty-family convention Ω and finite indexing remain parent-specific, not intrinsic to binary intersection.

Intermediate subfield k⊆L⊆K is an ordinary subfield L of K with inherited operations, together with the additional lower inclusion of k. This shares the subfield prerequisite in extension/prime-subfield sources, not the parent intermediate-field containment or algebraicity.

The coefficient-ring source uses pΛ, the principal ideal of Λ generated by the image of integer p. The general principal ideal (p) in a ring is exactly the same generated-ideal construction, while residue-characteristic and maximal-ideal intersection remain parent-specific.

The geometric-irreducibility source uses A⊗_k K for a commutative unital k-algebra A and field extension K/k. The connected-component source selects a connected subset C inclusion-maximal among connected subsets of X. The étale-ring-map source uses H_1(C•)=ker(d_1)/im(d_2) for a naive cotangent chain complex, exactly the i=1 specialization of H_i(C•)=ker(d_i)/im(d_{i+1}) recorded in the Tor-from-free-resolution source. In the syntomic-ring-map source the fibre algebra S⊗_R κ(p) is the exact base-change commutative R′-algebra construction S⊗_R R′ used in the universal-homeomorphism source, specialized to the R-algebra R′=κ(p). The topological pointwise-convergence source uses the function set T^D={f:D→T}, canonically identical to the set-theoretic Cartesian product ∏_{d∈D}T of a constant indexed family. The separably-generated-extension source's k(B), with B a potentially infinite transcendence basis over k, is a rational-function field in algebraically independent indeterminates B. Depth source takes the supremum of nonnegative lengths of M-regular sequences contained in an ideal. The extended value ∞, restriction to M-regular sequences, and containment in I remain defining source-context qualifications.

The finite-module-dimension source takes suprema of lengths of prime chains in Supp_R(M). These are least upper bounds in ℕ∪{∞} just as for any subset of an ordered set, with +∞ for unbounded integer lengths. The prime-chain restriction and support of M are parent-specific and do not become part of the abstract supremum prerequisite.

A finite rank free left R-module R^n is the finite-index direct sum of copies of R and hence the n-element-basis case of the generic free left R-module R^{(I)}. The finite-rank/standard-basis requirements for rank and Lazard, finite-presentation and finite-projective sources remain parent-specific; a free module of arbitrary rank is not assumed finite or locally free by this alias.

The splitting-field source's extension generated by F together with all roots of P in E is the general field-generation construction F(B), taking B to be the subset of roots. Full splitting of P, root selection, and splitting-field minimality remain only in the parent construction.

Rational expressions in α describe that generated subfield; its single-generator restriction and the primitive-element assertion are parent-specific, not imposed on arbitrary generated fields.

A finitely generated intermediate field E=k(a_1,...,a_n) within K is the general generated-subfield k(B) construction for finite generator set B={a_1,...,a_n}. The source's finiteness of B, selected ambient intermediate field, and distinction from finite vector-space degree remain explicit parent-specific qualifications.

The Kummer-extension source uses K(α), a simple field generated from K by adjoining α, which is the general generated-subfield construction k(B) with base k=K and singleton B={α}. The algebraic equation α^n=a, associated hypotheses on roots of unity and Kummer structure are extra conditions of the parent, not consequences of field generation.

The representable-functor-on-schemes source invokes a natural isomorphism of contravariant Set-valued functors; the representable-covariant-functor source invokes a natural isomorphism of covariant Set-valued functors. Both require the identical abstract prerequisite: a natural transformation with natural inverse, equivalently a natural family of isomorphism components. Different domain categories, functor variance and Hom-functor formulas remain attached to their respective sources and are NOT conflated.

The scheme-size source takes a least upper bound of a set of cardinal numbers ordered by cardinal comparison. This shares only the abstract poset supremum construction sup(A) as least upper bound with other ordered-set sources. The ambient order here is the cardinal order (not the ordered reals), the values are cardinals and the result is a cardinal supremum, all retained as source-specific typing; no cardinal/real-value identification is asserted.

The total-quotient-ring source localizes R at the set S of its non-zero-divisors. Requiring S to be all regular elements, rather than an arbitrary multiplicative subset, remains source-specific and is not generalized.

The topology-subbasis source forms finite intersections of open subbasic sets, including the empty finite intersection X. Openness of each member, closure under intersections and basis generation are parent-specific, not intrinsic to a set intersection.

The geometrically integral algebra source uses commutative unital scalar extension A⊗_k K for a field extension K/k, with exactly the same tensor-product K-algebra multiplication and canonical scalar structure as the previously consolidated R⊗_k K prerequisite (A and R are variable labels). The Dedekind-domain factorization characterization requires a finite iterated product P_1⋯P_n of ideals with the same finite-sums-of-products construction as the binary ideal product IJ, including R as the empty product. The locally-ringed-space definition uses the stalk O_{X,x} at every point x, which is precisely the sheaf-theoretic filtered colimit of sections on neighborhoods used in the reduced-scheme source's stalk prerequisite. The split-fibred-category source uses an isomorphism of categories over C with inverse over C. The category-fibred-in-sets source invokes the ordinary covariant functor p:E→C from total category to base category without assumed smallness. The left-adjoint source uses ordinary functors L:C→D and R:D→C, differing only in domain/codomain orientation and naming from a generic identity/composition-preserving functor. The presheaf-fibre-product source requires two natural transformations F⇒G and H⇒G between contravariant set-valued presheaves, with component maps compatible with restriction. In the finite-module support and irreducible-component sources, a Zariski-closed subset of Spec(R) has the form V(I)={p in Spec(R): I⊆p}. The locally-ringed-space morphism source's compatible structure-sheaf morphism for continuous f:X→Y is the ordinary ring-sheaf map O_Y→f_*O_X, equivalently via sheaf adjunction f^{-1}O_Y→O_X, as stated in the scheme-morphism source. Locally finite families and local Krull dimension take an open neighbourhood U of x, namely x∈U∈τ_X. The split-fibred-category source posits a base category C without a smallness hypothesis. The interval-weight formulation defines orthogonality of distinct-degree p_n,p_m by ∫p_n(x)p_m(x)w(x)dx=0 for n≠m, with nonnegative integrable weight and finite absolute moments. On the stated interval, define μ_w(B)=∫_{B∩(a,b)} w(x)dx; then dμ_w=w(x)dx and the two displayed orthogonality prerequisites coincide exactly. In the measure source μ may be more general (including singular Lebesgue–Stieltjes parts), so the measure-level prerequisite is the valid common abstraction; weights, density/absolute continuity, support, admissibility and moments remain distinctly specified in the full parent formulations. No claim that arbitrary μ must possess density w.
